In summary, our research is concerned with

a new paradigm of CR precoding design that exploits the noncausal information on the interference at the CR base station to improve the performance of the secondary link, while guaranteeing that the interference in the primary network is below a given threshold.

the design of novel transmit precoding schemes for the CR downlink, which exploit the noncausal information of interference in order to maximize the performance of secondary users while guaranteeing the quality of service of primary users.
the design of transmit precoding for the underlay CR Z-channel.

the proposed precoding schemes are capable of improving the performance of the secondary link, and hence the QoS of the secondary users, while maintaining the QoS of both the primary link and the secondary link.
the proposed methods provide a significant performance improvement over the conventional methods while guaranteeing the instantaneous QoS of primary and secondary users.
the proposed transmit precoding approaches are able to improve significantly the average QoS of secondary users, while satisfying the QoS of the primary users on an instant basis.

the proposed methods offer a new way to design the CR precoders to exploit the interference in the CR Z-channel, and thus improve the performance of secondary users while guaranteeing the instantaneous QoS of primary links.
